To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MHC class I gene product is a functional component of the receptor for IL-2.
the MHC class I antigen is of importance for the expression of IL-2 and -4 receptor function and that these two receptors are functionally linked.
MHC class I antigens are of importance for IL-2/IL-4 responsiveness in T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the functional expression of MHC molecules and lymphokine receptors.
the functional interactions between T-cell activation molecules, the TCR, the IL-2 receptor, MHC class I and II, and adhesion molecules.
the regulation of the expression of the receptors and the functional interactions between the lymphokine receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MHC class I antigen is a necessary component of the IL-2 and the IL-4 receptor complex and that IL-2 and/or IL-4 may act as an important regulator of class I expression on lymphoid cells.
MHC class I and II molecules are important for the regulation of lymphocyte activation, and that the regulation involves the receptors for IL2 and IL4.
class I molecules, IL-2 receptor, IL-3 receptor, and IL-3 are functionally linked in a complex regulatory network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
class I molecules play an important role in lymphokine responsiveness of T cells and in lymphokine interactions.
class I molecules and IL-2 receptors are functionally linked in the T-cell activation process.
class I molecules play a regulatory role in T-cell activation, and that the receptors for ILs 2 and 4 are functionally linked.
The main takeaway from our work is that
class I molecules play a critical role in the regulation of IL-2 and/or IL-4 receptor function.

the expression of IL-2R and IL-4R on the cell surface depends on MHC class I expression, and this dependence is not restricted to T-cells, but also applies to T-cell clones, T-cell lines, and T-lymphomas.
the expression of the IL-2 receptor is regulated by class I molecules, and that the expression of class I molecules is regulated by the IL-2 and the IL-4 receptor.
